newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine president appoints banker top reform chief.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine president appoints banker top reform chief.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma on Tuesday appointed Sergei Tigipko, head of a big commercial bank, as deputy prime minister in charge of reforms, the president's press secretary told Reuters.

"There is a decree appointing Tigipko as deputy prime minister," spokesman Dmitro Markov said. He added that the decree did not outline Tigipko's duties but the appointment followed the resignation of Viktor Pynzenyk last week from the post of deputy prime minister in charge of economic reforms.

Markov said that Tigipko, 37, head of Privatbank, one of Ukraine's top five banks, was a metallurgist by education from the central industrial city of Dnipropetrovsk where Kuchma once ran the Soviet Union's largest missile plant.

Tigipko has worked in banking since 1990, making Privatbank one of Ukraine's most profitable banks and pushing its starting capital to 30 million hryvnias ($16.5 million) at the end of 1996 from 10 million hryvnias a year earlier.
Tigipko's predecessor Pynzenyk, a dedicated reformer, quit in anger last Wednesday, saying he did not believe he could do any more to get this year's budget and tax reforms approved.
Pynzenyk, whose resignation Kuchma accepted only on Monday, accused parliament and government of lacking the political will to get the reforms passed.
